title: Task: a promise of a result
sub: A claim ticket instead of the answer
cards/0/title: A Task is a claim ticket
cards/0/body:
A Task is an object meaning "work that will finish later". Think of a dry cleaner's ticket: your clothes aren't ready yet, but you hold a slip you'll trade for them later.

A Task<string> is a ticket you'll trade for a string.
cards/1/body: A task can be in progress, completed successfully, faulted with an error, or canceled.
cards/1/deep: TaskStatus: Created, WaitingForActivation, WaitingToRun, Running, WaitingForChildrenToComplete, RanToCompletion, Canceled, Faulted. Tasks from async methods and I/O are usually WaitingForActivation: they aren't "running" on any thread, and something outside will complete them.
cards/2/pairs/1/1: The same, with an int result
cards/3/q: A method returned Task<string>. Where is the string?
cards/3/options/0: It may not exist yet: await hands it over when the task completes
cards/3/explain: A task is a promise. The result appears when the operation finishes.
cards/4/body:
Task.Run(() => …) hands work to a thread-pool thread. Use it for heavy computation so the main thread stays free.

I/O doesn't need Task.Run: GetStringAsync already doesn't hold a thread.
cards/4/deep: Task.Run(async () => …) unwraps the inner task correctly. Task.Factory.StartNew with an async lambda returns Task<Task>, and await then waits only for the start. A classic mistake.
cards/5/q: You need to compress a large image without freezing the window. What do you do?
cards/5/options/1: Call Compress(img) directly in the handler
cards/5/explain: Compression is CPU work. Task.Run moves it to the pool, and await brings the result back to the UI thread.
cards/6/q: Should you wrap http.GetStringAsync(url) in Task.Run?
cards/6/options/0: No: the request doesn't hold a thread anyway; Task.Run just ties up a pool thread
cards/6/options/1: Yes, or it will block the window
cards/6/explain: Async I/O already doesn't block. Task.Run on top is wasted work.
cards/7/q: How can a task end? Select all that apply.
cards/7/explain: Those are the three final states. You can't pause a task.
cards/8/q: Get the result without blocking the thread
cards/8/explain: await "unwraps" a Task<string> into a string.
